title: May I come in?
title_target: ဝင်လို့ ရလား — wiⁿ-loh. ya.-la:
goal: Asking permission, saying what you can do, and saying what you must do — four small words that sit in the same place in the sentence and often get mixed up by beginners.
bekal: asking permission with …လို့ ရလား
telling apart နိုင် (able to) and တတ် (know how to)
saying you must with …ရမယ်
saying what you want with …ချင်

dialogs.title: စကားပြော — Asking for time off at the office
dialogs.intro: Ani needs permission to leave early on Friday. Watch for four small words taking turns: ရ for permission, နိုင် for ability, တတ် for skill, and ရမယ် for obligation.

lines.speaker: အာနီ:
lines.text: [ဒေါ်ခင်|dò-hkiⁿ]၊ [ဝင်|wiⁿ] [လို့|loh.] [ရ|ya.] [လား|la:]။
lines.id: Daw Khin, may I come in?

lines.speaker: ဒေါ်ခင်:
lines.text: [ရ|ya.] [ပါတယ်|ba-dè]၊ [ဝင်|wiⁿ] [ပါ|ba]။ [ဘာ|ba] [ကိစ္စ|kayk-sa.] [လဲ|lè:]။
lines.id: Yes, please come in. What can I do for you?
lines.literal: may — polite-statement, enter — polite. what — matter — Q?

lines.speaker: အာနီ:
lines.text: [သောကြာနေ့|thaw-cha-nay.] [စော|sò] [ပြန်|pyaⁿ] [လို့|loh.] [ရ|ya.] [မလား|ma.la:]။

lines.text: [ဗလီ|ba.lee] [သွား|thwa:] [ရ|ya.] [မယ်|mè]။ [နေ့လယ်|nay.-lè] [ဆွမ်း|hswaⁿ:] [ဝတ်ပြု|wak-pyoo.] [ရ|ya.] [တယ်|dè]။

lines.text: [ဟုတ်ကဲ့|hohk-kè.]၊ [နားလည်|na:-lè] [ပါတယ်|ba-dè]။ [ဘယ်နှစ်နာရီ|bè-hna.na-yee] [ထွက်|htwèk] [ရ|ya.] [မ|ma.] [လဲ|lè:]။

grammars.title: …လို့ ရလား — asking permission
body: The permission pattern is **verb + လို့ + ရ**. ရ (*ya.*) means "get, receive, be allowed", and လို့ (*loh.*) links it to the verb in front.

head: Burmese
Say it
Meaning
rows: ဝင်လို့ ရလား
ဓာတ်ပုံ ရိုက်လို့ ရလား

after: ⚠️ ရ has many meanings and you'll meet them all: "may" (ဝင်လို့ရလား), "must" (သွားရမယ်), "get" (ငါး ရတယ် — caught a fish), and "manage to" (မရဘူး — couldn't manage). Its place in the sentence decides the meaning, and each use is covered separately in this book.

grammars.title: ⚠️ နိုင် vs တတ် — two kinds of "can"
body: English uses one word, "can", for two very different things: you can because **circumstances allow it**, and you can because **you've learned how**. Burmese keeps them apart, and swapping them is a mistake people notice right away.

head: Word
Say it
Meaning
Example
rows: မနက်ဖြန် လာနိုင်တယ် — I can come tomorrow
မြန်မာစကား ပြောတတ်တယ် — I can speak Burmese
ဝင်လို့ ရတယ် — you may come in

after: The test is simple: if the ability was **learned** — speaking a foreign language, swimming, cooking, riding a motorbike — use တတ်. If it depends on **circumstances** — having time, being strong enough, being up to it — use နိုင်.
An example to make it clear: ရေကူးတတ်တယ် means "I can swim" (I've learned how). ရေကူးနိုင်တယ် means "I'm able to swim right now" — say, because the water isn't too cold. Two sentences, two meanings.

grammars.title: …ရမယ် — must
body: Obligation is formed by slotting ရ in before the sentence ending. This one form covers "must", "have to", and "be forced to" all at once.

head: Burmese
Say it
Meaning
rows: ဘယ်နှစ်နာရီ ထွက်ရမလဲ
what time do you have to leave?
မလုပ်လည်း ရတယ်
you don't have to do it

after: ⚠️ Note that **မ…ရဘူး means "mustn't"**, not "don't have to". For "don't have to", use မလုပ်လည်း ရတယ် ("not doing it is also okay"). This matters: saying မသွားရဘူး to someone forbids them to go — it doesn't let them off.

grammars.title: …ချင် — want to
body: ချင် (*hchiⁿ*) attaches straight to the verb and expresses a wish. You've seen it since unit 2, and now it's time to use it in every form.

head: Burmese
Say it
Meaning
rows: သွားချင်တယ်
မသွားချင်ဘူး
ဘာ စားချင်လဲ
what do you want to eat?
ရေ သောက်ချင်တယ်

after: The full make-up of a Burmese verb at A1 level is: **verb + ချင်/နိုင်/တတ်/ရ + နေ/ခဲ့ + ending**. Everything attaches in order without changing the verb, and you can stack them: သွားချင်နေတယ် (am wanting to go), မသွားနိုင်သေးဘူး (can't go yet).

sections.title: Asking and refusing without giving offense

blocks.text: Burmese pays close attention to how you say anything that might inconvenience someone. The sentences below are the basic toolkit, and all of them are built from the four words you've just learned.

head: Burmese
Say it
English
rows: would it be okay to … later?
အားနာပါတယ်
not yet possible, not allowed yet
မအားလို့ပါ
နောက်မှ ရမလား
could we do it another time?

blocks.title: ⚠️ အားနာတယ် — a feeling with no English equivalent
items: **အားနာတယ်** (*a:-na-dè*) is the awkward feeling of putting someone out — a mix of embarrassment, reluctance, and gratitude. English has no single word for it; "I feel bad troubling you" comes closest. It matters just as much in daily life as any greeting.
Saying it when you accept help — အားနာပါတယ် — shows at once that you understand local manners, and people in Myanmar will feel much closer to you after hearing it.
Turning something down with **အားနာလို့ပါ** ("because I'd feel bad") is far gentler than giving the real reason, and no one will press you further.
